core.title: GREEN: smallest legal implementation of the failing acceptance
core.given: a governed ATDD task whose current behavioral acceptance is still RED
core.when: you write implementation code to make that acceptance pass
core.then: Write the smallest correct implementation that makes the current failing behavioral acceptance pass while respecting every active construction constraint.
prefer: Start from one failing behavioral acceptance. Keep the search on the missing behavior, and prefer a naturally simple implementation.
Reuse the nearest existing compliant contracts, components, dependencies and patterns. Implement the smallest path that makes the required behavior pass.
Add a new boundary or abstraction only when the current behavior actually needs it, that is, when no existing compliant path can express it.
Derive traceability metadata from the plan artifact and the acceptance. Do not invent it.

Treat the active construction-constraint rules as limits on a legal GREEN. They cover traceability and topology, architecture and dependency direction, runtime, design-system and responsive boundaries. Every other active profile, such as tester, traceability and security, is equally binding.

The implementation-identity traceability rules (implementation identity, proof, runtime, purpose, side and layer) are a traceability family, not a phase. Leave them where they are. They constrain GREEN.
Quality-metric sensor rules may run at any time, even while the acceptance is still RED, and they stay strict. Only your response changes with the phase.
Stop expanding scope once the acceptance passes and the construction constraints are satisfied.
avoid: Knowingly violating a construction constraint and planning to repair it later.
While RED: broadening the implementation just to optimize a quality metric, or gaming any finding.
While behavior is still being discovered: redesigning adjacent systems, generalizing for hypothetical callers, or doing unrelated cleanup.
Writing deliberately poor code. GREEN does not permit it.
Treating behavioral GREEN as the end of the coding loop.
unless: A narrow structural change may come before behavioral GREEN when the existing design makes the required behavior impossible to implement correctly. Preserve already-proven behavior and change only the verified blocker.
core.why: GREEN and REFACTOR are different search problems, and splitting them does not change enforcement. GREEN finds the smallest legal implementation of the required behavior. Construction constraints define what counts as legal while behavior is being discovered.
evidence: The acceptance was RED when GREEN started and now passes against the implementation (behavioral GREEN).
The GREEN change introduces no construction-constraint finding and no finding from another active profile.
The change reuses existing compliant paths. Any new boundary or abstraction is justified because no existing compliant path could express the behavior.
verification: Term behavioral_green: the point where the current RED behavioral acceptance passes against the implementation. It proves the requested behavior exists. It is not yet the end of the coding loop.

Term construction_constraint: a rule that constrains what counts as a legal implementation while behavior is being discovered. It covers traceability and topology, architecture and dependency direction, runtime, design-system and responsive boundaries, plus every other active non-refactor profile such as security.
No dedicated detector for this rule. Compliance is judged from phase ordering, acceptance runs and the results of the active convention profiles.
Enforcement does not change with the phase: construction-constraint and quality-sensor checks may run at any time and stay strict. Only the agent's response changes with the phase.

facts.note: Gate: governed coding work is driven by a behavioral acceptance.
Gate: the task is enrolled in the governed ATDD loop, its current behavioral acceptance is still RED, and implementation work is under way.
Hint only, not a gate. Task wording that places the work inside the governed ATDD loop; the rule applies even when the task wording contains none of these terms.

fires: The agent writes implementation code to make a failing behavioral acceptance pass.
A quality-metric sensor or construction-constraint finding appears while the acceptance is still RED.
doesNotFire: Work with no behavioral acceptance under the governed ATDD loop.
The acceptance has already passed. The REFACTOR and review-ready parts apply instead.

neutralityNotes: This is a process rule: its obligation, exceptions, evidence and activation gates are fully stack-neutral, so profileRequirements and proposedKeys are empty (the core references no path, idiom, root or tool). Gate/hint semantics are explicit at the core activation level: task_has_acceptance and phase are gates (each with its gate note, including the phase gate's governed-loop, still-RED, implementation-under-way explanation), while task_term is only a non-gating hint, so the rule applies even when the task wording lacks those terms. What could not be made neutral and stays bunOnly: the "Bun" stack qualifier in given; the detector/rule-id enumerations of the construction-constraint families in prefer[4], verifier_detail[1] and activation.facts[4]; the `green-*` rule-prefix family name in prefer[5]; the concrete seven-sensor quality family in prefer[6]; and the language activation hint in activation.facts[3], for which the closed neutral activation fact vocabulary has no language fact. In the core's verification, "the results of the active convention profiles" means the stack's active rule profiles, not the structure profile. Per-rule severity and disposition, and this rule's (absent) detector, are described generically in core:verification rather than as profile keys; bun.json remains the worked reference instantiation.
